title: Deal anchors and safety buffers — personal log
content:
Quick purpose: informal scratchpad for clause priorities, suggested micro-phrases for counters, and a short list of concession-and-fallback tradeoffs to keep on hand during calls. Not language for signatures — use legal-approved templates when escalating.

Context notes:
- Working an enterprise procurement for a regulated customer (financial services). They pushed hard on indemnity, data residency, and an absolute export-control carveout in the IP/license section.
- Internal ask: keep hosted inference as core; avoid on-prem carving unless paid. Need clear transition assistance and escrow triggers.
- Current negotiation pace: fast loop with AE + SE + buyer legal. I expect 2–3 redline rounds.

Priority clauses to flag (high -> low):
1) Indemnity (broadness): watch for open-ended negligence/third-party IP claims tied to customer data.
   - Trigger language to reject: "indemnify for all losses" with no cap, no gross negligence carveout.
   - Ask-for: narrow to third-party IP infringement claims arising from our deliverables; exclude customer data processing and any product usage outside documented API.

2) Data residency & export controls: buyer wants all production data stored in-region + export control clause that gives them full stop rights.
   - Redline: clarify "control plane" metadata vs. "customer content"; allow transient cross-region processing for load balancing and safety; provide commitment to region-at-rest where feasible (dedicated customers).
   - Export-control quick point: ensure clause requires reasonable notice and opportunity to remediate before service suspension.

3) License grant & use restrictions: avoid language that turns our models into customer-owned derivative work.
   - Insist on limited license for customer to use outputs in internal apps; we keep model weights and service rights.
   - If buyer asks for "sublicense/redistribute" language, require premium add-on and data export process.

4) Termination & transition assistance: must lock in 90 days minimum transition support for production customers; include escrow/exit pricing if they terminate without cause during an active commit.
   - Phrase: "30 days operation, 60 days transition assistance" is often the seller-favored split; push for 60/30 reversed in regulated deals.

5) SLA liability & cap: they ask for unlimited direct damages? nope. Push for negotiated cap = committed monthly fee x12 (common baseline), keep carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

6) Audit/Compliance: customer wants on-demand audits and broad access to logs.
   - Counter: quarterly reports + targeted audits by certified third party; require NDAs and scope limits; avoid direct-prod-console access.

Micro-phrases to use (short, conversational for negotiating with buyer counsel):
- "We can commit to region-at-rest for stored content; for real-time inference we need the flexibility to route for availability. We can add written guardrails or a dedicated deployment if this is a hard requirement."
- "For indemnities, our standard is to cover IP claims arising from the service — not for customer misuse of outputs or customer-supplied data processing choices."
- "We understand export concerns — we can commit to a notice-and-remediation process before any suspension tied to export controls. Immediate shutoff without coordination is operationally risky for both sides."
- "If you need relicense/redistribution rights that's a separate commercial discussion — we can add a license addendum for a different fee and controls."

Concessions we can make (and where to get value back):
- Offer: increased transition assistance window (60 days) in exchange for a higher termination fee or pro-rated commitment payment.
- Offer: limited audit rights (quarterly) if they accept SOC2/HIPAA attestation and sign an NDA for auditors.
- Offer: region-at-rest guarantee for dedicated customers only; hosted customers get best-effort with clear SLAs.
- Offer: escrow of minimal configuration + onboarding scripts (not model weights) as middle ground. Escrow for weights = expensive and rare; use only if significant MSP procurement demands it and compensated.

Escalation triggers (signals to pull in legal/exec):
- Buyer removes liability cap or demands uncapped indemnity.
- Buyer insists on model weight escrow or transfer of IP.
- Buyer requires full-console access for audit.
- Buyer demands on-prem source code as a contingency.
When these appear: escalate to VP Legal + Head of Sales; document business justification and potential revenue to offset risk.

Walkaway thresholds (my personal quick list):
- Uncapped liability for routine data breaches (not tied to willful misconduct) — walk if not insurable/mitigable.
- Requirement to provide model weights unless it's >$X ARR and explicit priced addendum.
- Indefinite data export without reasonable security/fees.

Short email snippets (copy-paste friendly) — use sparingly and edit tone: 
1) Region/export pushback: "We can accept region-at-rest for stored customer content. For live inference we need flexibility for routing; if region isolation is non-negotiable we can propose a dedicated deployment scoped in an appendix and priced accordingly."
2) Indemnity cap reply: "Our standard approach is to align liability caps with the committed fees; for enterprise commitments we are open to negotiate an uplift — please share the business reason and the expected ARR so we can route internally."
3) Escrow reply (if buyer persists): "Weights escrow is a high-friction step and generally reserved for very large, long-term commitments. Can we instead agree an escrow of configuration + model export instructions, plus extended transition assistance? If you can provide a commercial trigger (commitment level), we can escalate."

Chair's quick checklist before next call (my checklist):
- Confirm which deployment mode buyer expects (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Get rough ARR trigger they expect for special terms (weights/escrow/console access).
- Ask whether audit must be on-demand or periodic; who bears audit costs.
- Validate whether security attestations (SOC2/HIPAA) are sufficient as alternatives.

Open questions to resolve with legal team:
- Exact fallback language we accept for export-control suspensions (notice/time-to-remediate thresholds).
- Template escrow wording we are willing to offer for config vs weights.
- Liability cap multiple for enterprise (1x committed monthly * 12? 24?) — what is legal comfortable with?

Next steps / TODOs: 
- Draft three alternate redlines for indemnity: conservative (narrow), compromise (split risk), aggressive (we push back).
- Prep short talking points for AE + SE for customer call (two lines each).
- If buyer responds with weight-escrow ask, route to legal with revenue justification + proposed compensation.

Notes-to-self (brain-dump):
- Keep responses short on first pass; force buyer to explain the commercial reason for heavy asks. Often they fold when asked what problem is being solved.
- Use "we can consider as a paid add-on" language to convert legal asks into commercial levers.
- Document every concession to ensure downstream precedents are tracked.

End of scratchpad.

Revision log: 
- 2025-11-07: initial brain-dump.
- 2026-03-09: updated with standard micro-phrases and escalation thresholds (added export-control remediation language).
_note: informal personal doc — not legal advice
